about: What a session's fixed per-request cost is made of, and what a ten-problem batch cost, measured 2026-11-14 on an install built from the working tree (bootstrap: 40 extensions loaded, 0 failed), model Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8.

floor.method: ./pi --auto [flags] -p 'Say OK.' </dev/null in one empty project folder, then the largest input_tokens in .pi/sessions/*.jsonl; one run per row
floor.note: the rows overlap: a tool's definition and the prompt both mention it, so read each row as the size of a group, not an exact split

probes.label: `--fast`
probes.what: no npm-package tools at all: sub-agents, workflows, notebooks

batch.what: two sessions of ten stock coding problems (HumanEval-flavoured), the same ten prompts in the same order in each, one file per problem under solutions/
batch.check: imports all ten files and runs the cases each prompt states; proved on the seed (0/10) and on a reference solution (10/10) before any session ran
batch.defect: both project folders got solutions/__pycache__ - the session's python wrote bytecode into the user's project. Fixed in ./pi (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, tests/test_project.py), and the batch was run again on the fix: 20/20, no __pycache__

rerun_on_the_fix.install: bc10b, built from the tree carrying the PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE export

runs.error: read of solutions/p01.py before it was written: [E_NOT_FOUND]
